vt_black_mountain_north.blurb: Black Mountain North is a small cliff in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom, outside Norton and tucked beside a big rockfall under a powerline. It holds around fourteen routes, mostly single-pitch trad with a couple of sport lines, plus a few two-pitch outings. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to low 5.11, but the bulk sits between 5.8 and 5.10, which suits climbers stepping up to leading and confident beginners as well as intermediates. Expect a quiet, forested, off-the-radar feel rather than a crowded roadside wall. Descents are mostly walk-offs or downclimbs, and the trail in is short.
vt_black_mountain_north.parking_note: Head north on Route 114 for roughly three miles beyond Norton, turn onto Gaudette Road and follow the powerline road to a pullout just after a culvert, on the east side.
vt_black_mountain_north.approach: From the pullout, a freshly flagged trail leads to the left end of the cliff.
